summary: The article provides a generally accurate overview of Micron's Q3 FY2026 earnings and guidance, along with relevant information for Indian investors, but contains some inaccuracies regarding tax implications and dates.

claims.claim: Micron Technology reported record-breaking Q3 FY2026 results, with revenue of $41.46 billion and adjusted EPS of $25.11, significantly exceeding analyst expectations.
claims.note: Micron Technology reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $41.46 billion and non-GAAP adjusted EPS of $25.11, exceeding analyst estimates.

claims.claim: Micron's strong Q4 FY2026 guidance, projecting $50 billion in revenue and $31.00 adjusted EPS, further indicates a sustained AI-driven growth cycle and tight supply conditions.
claims.note: Micron provided Q4 FY2026 guidance of approximately $50 billion in revenue and $31.00 adjusted EPS.

claims.claim: For foreign stocks and ETFs held directly, if the investment is held for more than 24 months, it is considered a Long-Term Capital Gain (LTCG) and taxed at 12.5% without indexation benefit.
claims.note: Long-term capital gains on foreign stocks (held over 24 months) are taxed at 12.5% without indexation benefit.

claims.claim: For Indian mutual funds or FoFs that invest primarily in foreign stocks, the tax rules have changed. For units bought after April 1, 2023, any capital gains are taxed at your income tax slab rate, regardless of the holding period, until March 31, 2025. From April 1, 2025, if units are held for 24 months or more, LTCG will be taxed at 12.5% without indexation. STCG (held for less than 24 months) will be taxed at the slab rate.
claims.note: For units bought after April 1, 2023, capital gains are taxed at the slab rate regardless of holding period until April 1, 2025. From April 1, 2025, if held for 24 months or more, LTCG is taxed at 12.5% without indexation; STCG (less than 24 months) is taxed at the slab rate.

claims.claim: Dividends received from US stocks are subject to a 25% withholding tax in the US. However, due to the Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (DTAA) between India and the US, Indian investors can claim this tax paid in the US as a foreign tax credit when filing their income tax returns in India, avoiding double taxation. Dividends are taxable in India as "Income from Other Sources" at your applicable slab rate.
claims.note: Dividends from US stocks are subject to a 25% withholding tax in the US, which can be claimed as a foreign tax credit in India under DTAA. Dividends are taxable in India as 'Income from Other Sources' at the applicable slab rate.

claims.claim: As per current regulations, Tax Collected at Source (TCS) is applicable on remittances made under the LRS. For remittances exceeding ₹10 lakh in a financial year, a TCS of 20% is levied for all categories other than education and medical treatment. This TCS amount can be adjusted against your overall income tax liability when filing your Income Tax Return (ITR).
claims.note: As of April 1, 2026, for LRS remittances exceeding ₹10 lakhs in a financial year, a TCS of 20% is levied for purposes other than education and medical treatment. This TCS is adjustable against income tax liability.

claims.claim: Anjali remits ₹15,00,000 (approx. $18,000) under LRS. Since this amount exceeds ₹10 lakhs, a 20% TCS is applicable on the amount exceeding ₹10 lakhs. Amount exceeding ₹10 lakhs = ₹15,00,000 - ₹10,00,000 = ₹5,00,000. TCS @ 20% on ₹5,00,000 = ₹1,00,000. This ₹1,00,000 can be claimed as a credit when filing her ITR.
claims.note: For LRS remittances exceeding ₹10 lakhs for purposes other than education and medical treatment, a 20% TCS is applicable on the amount exceeding ₹10 lakhs. This TCS can be claimed as a credit.
